messages:
maya: Heads-up — fleet saturation spikes on us during EMEA morning. Thinking about switching from per-key token-bucket refill to a hybrid 'fairshare + priority reserve' approach. Thoughts?

derek: Which pools are getting hammered? any single-org blast?

maya: gpu-pool-eu-1 and some preemptible us-west nodes. 95th pct GPU util ~92% for the last 3 hours. Queue depth up ~6x. Root cause looks like a sustained burst from org:streamlytics.

sophia: I like fairshare but we need bounded burst. Proposal: keep per-key token-buckets for steady-state, but add a shared capacity pool that can lend tokens when per-key buckets are exhausted; lending rate driven by queue length and cluster free capacity.

maya: Sketch of config:

```
per_key_bucket: capacity=1000, refill=10/s
org_bucket: capacity=10000, refill=80/s
shared_pool: dynamic_refill = free_capacity * alpha
priority_reserve: small fixed reserve for high-SLA orgs
```

sophia: How do we compute free_capacity? node_free_gpu_slots? or translate into token/sec based on model throughput?

derek: free_capacity = max(0, target_util - current_util) * max_throughput. Use EWMA smoothing on current_util. If cluster_util > 90% we immediately disable lending and move to hard caps/fail-open? fail-closed?

audrey: Prefer graceful degradation: when lending disabled, either 429 with x-rw-rl-reason or auto-degrade to cheaper model (e.g., gpt-small) and attach header for caller to log. Better UX than silent 429s.

maya: Agree on degrade path. Also important: region isolation — lending should be regional (no cross-region token borrowing) to respect latency and data placement.

ken: Persistence question: rate-limit state after service restart. If we persist every token change it's heavy. We can accept small drift but need monotonic guarantees to avoid double-spend.

sophia: We could do in-memory counters with periodic checkpoint to etcd + monotonic refill on restart (reconstruct by last_checkpoint + elapsed_time * refill_rate). That accepts drift on crashes but keeps implementation light.

maya: UX headers: x-rw-rl-remaining, x-rw-rl-limit, x-rw-rl-reason. Also an admin /quota/status endpoint showing borrow balance and estimated repay time per org.

infra-bot: incident-bot: queue-depth(eu) crossed 500 at 2026-12-04T08:21:10Z — automated backpressure engaged.

deploy-bot: rolling canary of rl-service/priority-fairshare starting in prod-eu in 10m :rocket:

derek: Test plan: simulate 10k concurrent streams from a single org and ensure fairshare doesn't allow long-tail starvation. Also test priority reserve to confirm high-SLA org keeps minimal throughput.

audrey: Cost note: lending from shared_pool might increase overall GPU cycles (more churn). Tie lending budget to billing plan / credit meter so free-tier orgs can't borrow indefinitely. Emit borrow_cost metrics so billing can bill borrowed capacity.

sophia: Telemetry: per-org borrow/repay counters, borrow_rate, borrow_latency, lending_disabled_events. Dashboards for cluster-level lending utilization vs free_capacity.

maya: I'll draft a PR with config knobs (alpha, reserve_size, lending_thresholds, fallback_model_map) + runbook. Want a canary script too — who pairs on chaos tests and persistence?

ken: I'll take chaos tests and help hammer the persistence checkpointing approach.

derek: I'll add admission-controller hooks to flip lending off when queue_depth > threshold and a test for spike-recovery.

maya: Great. Going to write the PR and include the config examples + sample header semantics. Thanks all.

deploy-bot: canary started for rl-service/priority-fairshare in prod-eu (instance 3/10) :eyes:

maya: keeping an eye — will post observability links once dashboards are up.
